name: echelongraph-mcp
description: CVE, KEV, EPSS, SBOM and advisory lookups; per-CVE exposure from Shodan data (© Shodan). Keyless.
long_description:
CVE and internet-exposure data for Claude, Cursor, Cline, and any MCP client, from EchelonGraph's free public feed: NVD, MITRE-CNA pre-NVD records, CISA-KEV, EPSS and GitHub GHSA, plus a per-CVE internet-exposure footprint: how many internet-facing services (distinct ip:port) EchelonGraph's KEV-exposure radar has on record running a version that maps to the CVE. Exposure counts are derived from Shodan data. Shodan data is owned by Shodan, which holds its copyright (© Shodan).

Free and keyless: no API key, no auth, read-only. The server makes no request other than the API call a tool needs to answer. Every result carries a structured envelope (state, measured_at, method, coverage, freshness, notes), and a CVE outside the exposure radar's tracked set is reported as not assessed, not as zero.

tools.name: epss_history
tools.description: EPSS change history for one CVE

tools.name: check_affected
tools.description: Am I affected? (product or package at a version)

tools.name: check_sbom
tools.description: Check an SBOM against the advisory corpus

tools.name: scan_manifest
tools.description: Check a lockfile against the advisory corpus

prompts.name: triage_cve
prompts.description: Triage one CVE: get_cve (with CISA's due date when the CVE is KEV-listed), cve_intel, cve_remediation, vendor_advisories_for_cve, epss_history and cve_exposure, then a decision template: exploited, likelihood, reachable, patch, deadline. Each line cites its tool and measured_at, and not_assessed is never reported as clean.
prompts.text: Triage ${arguments.cve_id} with the EchelonGraph MCP tools: get_cve, cve_intel, cve_remediation, vendor_advisories_for_cve, epss_history and cve_exposure, then answer exploited, likelihood, reachable, patch, deadline and decision, one line each, citing the tool and measured_at behind each line. Report not_assessed as not assessed, never as clean.

prompts.name: kev_weekly_brief
prompts.description: A brief of the CVEs CISA added to its KEV catalog in the last N days (default 7): kev_recent from a since date the model computes from days, grouped by vendor, with ransomware flags and due dates, dated by EchelonGraph's last successful fetch of CISA's feed.
prompts.text: Write a brief of the CVEs CISA added to its Known Exploited Vulnerabilities (KEV) catalog in the last ${arguments.days} days (7 when not given), using the EchelonGraph MCP tool kev_recent from that date, paged with next_cursor: grouped by vendor, with ransomware flags and due dates, dated by measured_at, EchelonGraph's last successful fetch of CISA's feed. If kev_recent failed, say the catalog could not be read, never that nothing was added.

prompts.name: am_i_affected
prompts.description: Whether a product (its NVD CPE product token) or a registry package (ecosystem and package) at a version is affected by known CVEs: check_affected, read assessed before count, with the not-assessed wording: a count of 0 under assessed false is never reported as not affected.
prompts.text: Check with the EchelonGraph MCP tool check_affected whether this is affected by known CVEs: product ${arguments.product}, or ecosystem ${arguments.ecosystem} and package ${arguments.package}, at version ${arguments.version}. Read assessed before count: a count of 0 under assessed false is not assessed, never not affected.

prompts.name: sbom_review
prompts.description: Review an SBOM (CycloneDX JSON or SPDX JSON text, up to 5000000 characters): it is passed to check_sbom, which checks up to 2000 distinct purls per call in batches of 200, then get_cve and cve_intel for each affected CVE, and a prioritised fix list ordered by CISA-KEV listing, then EPSS, then score, each key stated, with each fixed version read from check_sbom's fixed_in where a match carries it, and cve_remediation's vendor remediation for the first 5 CVEs. undetermined and not_assessed components are listed as not checked, never as clean.
prompts.text:
Review the SBOM below for known vulnerabilities with the EchelonGraph MCP tools: pass it to check_sbom, look up each affected CVE with get_cve and cve_intel, and write a fix list ordered by CISA-KEV listing, then EPSS, then score, giving each fixed version from the match's fixed_in. List the undetermined and not_assessed components as not checked, never as clean.

${arguments.sbom}

prompts.name: workload_triage
prompts.description: Rank your own pods, CI job containers or images against EchelonGraph's advisory corpus and CISA's KEV catalog: you list the workloads and decide their exposure with your own tools, make an SBOM of each image digest, and pass check_sbom the purls alone; rows are ordered by CISA-KEV listing, then caller-asserted exposure, then EPSS, then score. not_assessed rows are counted and never reported as clean. The prompt takes no workload data.
prompts.text: Triage the container workloads I run (listed in ${arguments.source}: kubernetes, github_actions or images) against EchelonGraph's advisory corpus and CISA's KEV catalog: list them and decide their exposure with your own tools, labelled caller-asserted, make an SBOM of each image digest, and pass check_sbom the purls alone, with no workload, image or registry name. Order them by CISA-KEV listing, then exposure, then EPSS, then score, and never report not_assessed rows as clean.
